<context>
You are an expert at solving ARC-AGI (Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus) puzzles using Answer Set Programming (ASP).

ARC-AGI puzzles show input-output grid transformations. Each cell contains a color value (integer 0–9). The goal is to discover the hidden transformation rule from training examples and encode it as an ASP program.
</context>

<rules>
- `input(row, col, color)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- `color(0..9)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- the output predicate is always `output(row, col, color)` — do not redefine it.
- the final program must produce exactly one answer set, in which `output(row, col, color)` match the expected output exactly.
- end your program with `#show output/3.`
</rules>

<example_1>
This puzzle copies the input to the output unchanged.

<grid_1>
Input:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>
</grid_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Copy each input cell to the output unchanged
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, C, Color).

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.

col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

</asp>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input

% Each output cell gets exactly one color

% Mirror: column C of the output is column (M-1-C) of the input.
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, Cin, Color), n_cols(M), C = M - 1 - Cin.

#show output/3.
</asp>

   * If a colour occurs only once (or only once in a column) we fall back to the *global* periods – this yields the periodic pattern seen in the examples (e.g. 2 and 8 with period 4, 1 and 3 with period 6, 2/3 with period 10).  
   In both cases the derived rule forces the colour to appear exactly at the positions `(row = base_row + k·rowPeriod,  col = base_col + l·colPeriod)`. Because the base rows, base columns and the periods are different for every colour, a cell can satisfy at most one colour – the choice rule then picks that colour, and cells that satisfy none keep colour 0.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Grid dimensions and cell set
% ------------------------------------------------------------
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).
output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Colours
% ------------------------------------------------------------
color(0..9).

% Exactly one colour per cell (choice rule)
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Helper predicates – smallest row/column for a colour
% ------------------------------------------------------------
% smallest row where colour C occurs
base_row(Row,Color) :-
    input(Row,_,Color),
    not exists R2 : input(R2,_,Color), R2 < Row.

% smallest column where colour C occurs
base_col(Col,Color) :-
    input(_,Col,Color),
    not exists C2 : input(_,C2,Color), C2 < Col.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Periods (global – the same for all colours)
% ------------------------------------------------------------
%   a colour that occurs in at least two different rows gives a row period
row_period(Period) :-
    input(R1,_,C),                     % colour C appears at row R1
    input(R2,_,C), R2 > R1,            % colour C appears again at row R2
    not exists R3 : input(R3,_,C), R3 > R1, R3 < R2,
    Period = R2 - R1.
row_period(P) :-
    not exists row_period(P),           % no colour with two rows → default 1
    P = 1.

%   a colour that occurs in at least two different columns gives a column period
col_period(Period) :-
    input(_,C1,Col), input(_,C2,Col), C2 > C1,          % colour C appears at columns C1 and C2
    not exists C3 : input(_,C3,Col), C3 > C1, C3 < C2,
    Period = C2 - C1.
col_period(P) :-
    not exists col_period(P),           % no colour with two columns → default 1
    P = 1.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Output for each colour
% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  (a) colours that have at least two rows *and* two columns
output(R,C,Col) :-
    base_row(R1,Col),                     % smallest row for this colour
    base_col(C1,Col),                     % smallest column for this colour
    second_row(R2,Col),                   % second (next) row for this colour
    col_period(ColPeriod),                % column period – may be global
    row_period(RowPeriod),                % row period – may be global
    R = R1 + K*RowPeriod,
    C = C1 + L*ColPeriod,
    K >= 0, L >= 0,
    R < N, C < M.

%  (b) colours that have only one row (or one column)
output(R,C,Col) :-
    base_row(R1,Col),
    base_col(C1,Col),
    row_period(RowPeriod),                % will be the global row period (1 if no other rows)
    col_period(ColPeriod),                % will be the global column period (1 if no other columns)
    R = R1 + K*RowPeriod,
    C = C1 + L*ColPeriod,
    K >= 0, L >= 0,
    R < N, C < M.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
#show output/3.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Grid dimensions
% ------------------------------------------------------------
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.

row(R)   :- R >= 0, R < N.
col(C)   :- C >= 0, C < M.
output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Find the two non‑zero cells (different colours) in reading order
% ------------------------------------------------------------
first(R1, C1, Col1) :-
    input(R1, C1, Col1), Col1 != 0,
    not exists R2, C2, Col' : input(R2, C2, Col'),
          (R2 < R1) or (R2 = R1, C2 < C1), Col' != 0.

second(R2, C2, Col2) :-
    input(R2, C2, Col2), Col2 != 0,
    Col2 != Col1,
    (R2 > R1) or (R2 = R1, C2 > C1),
    not exists R3, C3, Col'' : input(R3, C3, Col''),
          (R3 < R2) or (R3 = R2, C3 < C2), Col'' != 0.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Differences and orientation
% ------------------------------------------------------------
dr = R2 - R1.
dc = C2 - C1.

col_orient :- dc <= dr, dc != 0.
row_orient :- dr < dc, dr != 0.
row_orient :- dc = 0, dr != 0.

% exactly one orientation is used
col_orient_true :- col_orient.
row_orient_true :- row_orient.
1 { col_orient_true, row_orient_true } 1.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Period
% ------------------------------------------------------------
period(P) :-
    col_orient_true,
    dr > 0,
    (dr % 2 = 0, P = dr // 2)
    ;
    col_orient_true,
    dr > 0,
    dr % 2 != 0, P = dr - 1.

period(P) :-
    row_orient_true,
    dr > 0,
    P = dr * 2.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Offsets for the two colours
% ------------------------------------------------------------
offset1 = orient ? (C1 % P) : (R1 % P).            % not used directly – used in output definitions
offset2 = (offset1 + P // 2) % P.                % will be used in the start‑position constraints

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Start positions for the second colour
% ------------------------------------------------------------
startCol :: integer.
1 { startCol } 1 :-
    col_orient_true,
    startCol >= C2,
    startCol % P = (C1 % P + P // 2) % P,
    startCol < C2 + P.

startRow :: integer.
1 { startRow } 1 :-
    row_orient_true,
    startRow % P = (R1 % P + P // 2) % P,
    startRow < N.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Output for column orientation
output(R, C, Col1) :-
    col_orient_true,
    input(R, C, Col1),
    C >= C1,
    C % P = C1 % P.

output(R, C, Col2) :-
    col_orient_true,
    input(R, C, Col2),
    exists K : K >= 0, C = startCol + K * P, C < M.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Output for row orientation
output(R, C, Col1) :-
    row_orient_true,
    input(R, C, Col1),
    R >= R1,
    R % P = R1 % P.

output(R, C, Col2) :-
    row_orient_true,
    input(R, C, Col2),
    exists K : K >= 0, R = startRow + K * P, R < N.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Ensure exactly one colour per cell (zero if neither pattern applies)
support(R, C, Col) :-
    Col = 0,
    not exists Col2 : output(R, C, Col2), Col2 != 0.

support(R, C, Col) :-
    Col != 0,
    Col = Col1,
    output(R, C, Col1).

support(R, C, Col) :-
    Col != 0,
    Col != Col1,
    Col = Col2,
    output(R, C, Col2).

1 { output(R, C, Col) : color(Col), support(R, C, Col) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

#show output/3.

% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(R) :- R >= 0, R < N.
col(C) :- C >= 0, C < M.
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Colors (provided automatically)
color(0..9).

% Exactly one output per cell
1 { output(R, C, Col) : color(Col) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% For each color, find its first occurrence (minimum row, minimum column)
base_row(R0, Col) :-
    input(R0, _, Col),
    not exists R1 : input(R1, _, Col), R1 < R0.

base_col(C0, Col) :-
    input(_, C0, Col),
    not exists C1 : input(_, C1, Col), C1 < C0.

% Find second occurrence (next row/column) for a color, if any
second_row(R1, Col) :-
    base_row(R0, Col),
    input(R1, _, Col),
    R1 > R0,
    not exists R2 : input(R2, _, Col), R2 < R1, R2 > R0.

second_col(C1, Col) :-
    base_col(C0, Col),
    input(_, C1, Col),
    C1 > C0,
    not exists C2 : input(_, C2, Col), C2 < C1, C2 > C0.

% Period for a color: distance between first and second occurrence, else 1
row_period(P, Col) :-
    base_row(R0, Col),
    second_row(R1, Col),
    P = R1 - R0.

row_period(P, Col) :-
    base_row(R0, Col),
    not exists second_row(_, Col),
    P = 1.

col_period(P, Col) :-
    base_col(C0, Col),
    second_col(C1, Col),
    P = C1 - C0.

col_period(P, Col) :-
    base_col(C0, Col),
    not exists second_col(_, Col),
    P = 1.

% Generate output cells for each color using its period(s)
output(R, C, Col) :-
    base_row(R0, Col),
    base_col(C0, Col),
    row_period(Rp, Col),
    col_period(Cp, Col),
    R = R0 + K * Rp,
    C = C0 + L * Cp,
    K >= 0, L >= 0,
    R < N,
    C < M.

% For cells that are not covered by any colored period, force 0

    output_cell(R, C),
    not output(R, C, Col) : Col > 0.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Grid dimensions and basic helpers
% ------------------------------------------------------------
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(R)   :- R >= 0, R < N.
col(C)   :- C >= 0, C < M.
output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Colours (automatically present)
% ------------------------------------------------------------
color(0..9).

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Helper predicates for each colour
% ------------------------------------------------------------
% smallest row where colour C occurs
base_row(R0, C) :-
    input(R0, _, C),
    not exists R1 : input(R1, _, C), R1 < R0.

% smallest column where colour C occurs
base_col(C0, C) :-
    input(_, C0, C),
    not exists C1 : input(_, C1, C), C1 < C0.

% second (next) row where colour C occurs, if any
second_row(R1, C) :-
    base_row(R0, C),
    input(R1, _, C),
    R1 > R0,
    not exists R2 : input(R2, _, C), R2 < R1, R2 > R0.

% second (next) column where colour C occurs, if any
second_col(C1, C) :-
    base_col(C0, C),
    input(_, C1, C),
    C1 > C0,
    not exists C2 : input(_, C2, C), C2 < C1, C2 > C0.

% row period for a colour (distance to the next occurrence) – default 1
row_period(P, C) :-
    base_row(R0, C), second_row(R1, C), P = R1 - R0.
row_period(P, C) :-
    base_row(R0, C), not exists second_row(_, C), P = 1.

% column period for a colour (distance to the next occurrence) – default 1
col_period(P, C) :-
    base_col(C0, C), second_col(C1, C), P = C1 - C0.
col_period(P, C) :-
    base_col(C0, C), not exists second_col(_, C), P = 1.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Cells that belong to the periodic pattern of a colour
% ------------------------------------------------------------
output(R, C, Col) :-
    base_row(R0, Col),
    base_col(C0, Col),
    row_period(Rp, Col),
    col_period(Cp, Col),
    R = R0 + K * Rp,
    C = C0 + L * Cp,
    K >= 0, L >= 0,
    R < N,
    C < M,
    Col != 0.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Which colour a cell may receive?
%  (a) colour 0 – only if the cell is not covered by any non‑zero pattern
%  (b) colour >0 – only if the cell is covered by that colour’s pattern
% ------------------------------------------------------------
support(R, C, Col) :-
    Col = 0,
    not exists Col2 : color(Col2), Col2 != 0, output(R, C, Col2).

support(R, C, Col) :-
    Col != 0,
    output(R, C, Col).

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Exactly one colour per cell – the colour is forced by the
%  support predicate above
% ------------------------------------------------------------
1 { output(R, C, Col) : color(Col), support(R, C, Col) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

#show output/3.
</asp>

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Grid dimensions and basic helpers
% ------------------------------------------------------------
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(R)   :- R >= 0, R < N.
col(C)   :- C >= 0, C < M.
output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Colours (automatically present)
% ------------------------------------------------------------
color(0..9).

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Helper predicates for each colour
% ------------------------------------------------------------
% smallest row where colour C occurs
base_row(R0, C) :-
    input(R0, _, C),
    not exists R1 : input(R1, _, C), R1 < R0.

% smallest column where colour C occurs
base_col(C0, C) :-
    input(_, C0, C),
    not exists C1 : input(_, C1, C), C1 < C0.

% second (next) row where colour C occurs, if any
second_row(R1, C) :-
    base_row(R0, C),
    input(R1, _, C),
    R1 > R0,
    not exists R2 : input(R2, _, C), R2 < R1, R2 > R0.

% second (next) column where colour C occurs, if any
second_col(C1, C) :-
    base_col(C0, C),
    input(_, C1, C),
    C1 > C0,
    not exists C2 : input(_, C2, C), C2 < C1, C2 > C0.

% row period for a colour (distance to the next occurrence) – default 1
row_period(P, C) :-
    base_row(R0, C), second_row(R1, C), P = R1 - R0.
row_period(P, C) :-
    base_row(R0, C), not exists second_row(_, C), P = 1.

% column period for a colour (distance to the next occurrence) – default 1
col_period(P, C) :-
    base_col(C0, C), second_col(C1, C), P = C1 - C0.
col_period(P, C) :-
    base_col(C0, C), not exists second_col(_, C), P = 1.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Cells that belong to the periodic pattern of a colour
% ------------------------------------------------------------
output(R, C, Col) :-
    base_row(R0, Col),
    base_col(C0, Col),
    row_period(Rp, Col),
    col_period(Cp, Col),
    R = R0 + K * Rp,
    C = C0 + L * Cp,
    K >= 0, L >= 0,
    R < N,
    C < M,
    Col != 0.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Which colour a cell may receive?
%  (a) colour 0 – only if the cell is not covered by any non‑zero pattern
%  (b) colour >0 – only if the cell is covered by that colour’s pattern
% ------------------------------------------------------------
support(R, C, Col) :-
    Col = 0,
    not exists Col2 : color(Col2), Col2 != 0, output(R, C, Col2).

support(R, C, Col) :-
    Col != 0,
    output(R, C, Col).

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Exactly one colour per cell – the colour is forced by the
%  support predicate above
% ------------------------------------------------------------
1 { output(R, C, Col) : color(Col), support(R, C, Col) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

#show output/3.
</asp>

col(C)   :- C >= 0, C < M.

first(R1, C1, Col1) :-

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Differences and orientation
% ------------------------------------------------------------
dr = R2 - R1.
dc = C2 - C1.

col_orient :- dc <= dr, dc != 0.
row_orient :- dr < dc, dr != 0.
row_orient :- dc = 0, dr != 0.

% exactly one orientation is used
col_orient_true :- col_orient.
row_orient_true :- row_orient.
1 { col_orient_true, row_orient_true } 1.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Period
% ------------------------------------------------------------
period(P) :-
    col_orient_true,
    dr > 0,
    (dr % 2 = 0, P = dr // 2)
    ;
    col_orient_true,
    dr > 0,
    dr % 2 != 0, P = dr - 1.

period(P) :-
    row_orient_true,
    dr > 0,
    P = dr * 2.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Offsets for the two colours
% ------------------------------------------------------------
offset1 = orient ? (C1 % P) : (R1 % P).            % not used directly – used in output definitions
offset2 = (offset1 + P // 2) % P.                % will be used in the start‑position constraints

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Start positions for the second colour
% ------------------------------------------------------------
startCol :: integer.
1 { startCol } 1 :-
    col_orient_true,
    startCol >= C2,
    startCol % P = (C1 % P + P // 2) % P,
    startCol < C2 + P.

startRow :: integer.
1 { startRow } 1 :-
    row_orient_true,
    startRow % P = (R1 % P + P // 2) % P,
    startRow < N.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Output for column orientation
output(R, C, Col1) :-
    col_orient_true,
    input(R, C, Col1),
    C >= C1,
    C % P = C1 % P.

output(R, C, Col2) :-
    col_orient_true,
    input(R, C, Col2),
    exists K : K >= 0, C = startCol + K * P, C < M.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Output for row orientation
output(R, C, Col1) :-
    row_orient_true,
    input(R, C, Col1),
    R >= R1,
    R % P = R1 % P.

output(R, C, Col2) :-
    row_orient_true,
    input(R, C, Col2),
    exists K : K >= 0, R = startRow + K * P, R < N.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Ensure exactly one colour per cell (zero if neither pattern applies)
support(R, C, Col) :-
    Col = 0,
    not exists Col2 : output(R, C, Col2), Col2 != 0.

support(R, C, Col) :-
    Col != 0,
    Col = Col1,
    output(R, C, Col1).

support(R, C, Col) :-
    Col != 0,
    Col != Col1,
    Col = Col2,
    output(R, C, Col2).

1 { output(R, C, Col) : color(Col), support(R, C, Col) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

#show output/3.
